solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rent's rotten exploitation

blocks.note: a rent is a tear, also called a rip
food that is rotten has gone off

explanation.surface: A tenant grumbles that the rent charged is a scandalous exploitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Rent's rotten' as 'rip is off': the rent is a tear, not a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-off is an informal noun for a swindle or overcharging, which is exploitation of the buyer.

clue.text: Sandwich and drinks for all?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sandwich made from two whole slices of bread
second meaning: one person buying a drink for everyone in the group

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub offers to stand food and drinks for the whole table.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a single sandwich and a set of drinks bought for a group are called by this same noun in British usage.

clue.text: Herald Pope's first special decree

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word just before it
special suggests something specially made up, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the initial letter of Pope
the six letters of decree rearranged

explanation.surface: A herald announces the pontiff's first special decree to the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herald' looks like a noun in the scene but is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to come before it as a sign, so it is a verb synonym for going before.

clue.text: Frodo lay sick, admitting his leadership to be reckless

indicators.note: being sick is being out of sorts, so the letters are disordered
admitting means letting in, so one piece is taken inside the other
the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the letters of these two words taken together
the opening letter of his

explanation.surface: The hobbit Frodo, lying ill, still insists on leading in a rash way.
explanation.walkthrough: The H joins the eight letters of 'Frodo lay' and all nine are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy describes someone bold without thought for danger, a direct synonym of rash or reckless.

clue.text: Lined up when verbally prompted

indicators.note: verbally means in speech, so the word is identified by how it is said

blocks.note: an actor who is prompted is cued, which is pronounced like the spelling of the answer

explanation.surface: Actors waited in line, given their prompts by spoken signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To queue is to wait in a line, so having queued is having lined up.

clue.text: Some delegates publicised mounting disruption

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used
in a down clue mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A few delegates made public their growing disruption of the conference.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a noun for a disturbance or disruption of the normal order.

clue.text: Nursed wound putting on small strip

indicators.note: wound as in twisted round, so the letters are coiled into a different order

blocks.note: the six letters of nursed rearranged
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A nurse tends an injury and applies a small strip of plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury and 'strip' like a plaster, but wound is twisted and strip is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off one's clothes, the same verb sense as to undress.

clue.text: Catch up with faltering leader, clinching win and victory overall at last

indicators.note: faltering means stumbling, so the letters lose their order
at last points to the final letter of the word before it
clinching means gripping tightly, so the outer letters hold the others

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
W is the abbreviation for win in results tables
V for victory
the final letter of overall

explanation.surface: A challenger draws even with a race leader who is flagging, winning at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of 'leader' have W, V and L slotted between them at three points.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw level is an idiom for reaching the same position as a rival who was ahead, i.e. catching up.

clue.text: In France I import British TV and a record player

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: je is French for I
UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: Someone in France imports British televisions and a gramophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A jukebox is a coin-operated machine that plays chosen records, so it is a kind of record player.

clue.text: Employed help of motorists in review for second hand vehicle

indicators.note: reviewing is looking back over something, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: employed means put to use
the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British roadside breakdown service

explanation.surface: A motoring organisation's helpers review a pre-owned car before sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motoring organisation offering breakdown help to drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that has had a previous owner is a second-hand vehicle, the plain meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Home for Religious Education team with new church

blocks.note: RE is the school-subject abbreviation
a team is a side
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A house is found for a school religion teacher's team and a new church.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a formal word for the place where someone lives, i.e. a home.

clue.text: Phantom Menace is doing nothing and theatre shortened run

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the word loses its final letter
colours that run spread out of place, so the letters move around

blocks.note: doing nothing is being idle
taken as written, then cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: A review says the Star Wars film The Phantom Menace is inert and its theatre run cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last E of 'theatre', then rearrange what is left. The definition borrows the title of a Star Wars film.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace that is only a phantom is a threat never meant to be carried out, an empty warning.

clue.text: Imagine coming back carrying large fish

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the letters run the other way
carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: to imagine something is to see it in your mind
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Picture an angler returning home with a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, so the plural noun matches the plural sense of fish here.

clue.text: Complete vertical

blocks.note: first meaning: utter, as in a downright folly
second meaning: rising straight up, like a cliff face

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase about something wholly upright, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both absolute or utter and perpendicular or very steep.

clue.text: Extra issue arising in leisure hours

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means going upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: something extra is spare
to issue is to give out, or emit

explanation.surface: An additional problem crops up during someone's time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare time is the free period outside work, the same idea as leisure hours.

clue.text: Cutting uncontrolled vice and sin on island

indicators.note: uncontrolled means running wild, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: I is the map abbreviation for island
taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Rampant wickedness on an island is cut back hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on island' puts the jumbled letters after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisive literally means cutting into, and figuratively sharp or penetrating, as cutting remarks are.

clue.text: Enters race across lake and achieves

indicators.note: across means spanning over, so the outer word stretches round the inner letter

blocks.note: someone who enters a race competes
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An athlete takes part in a race over a lake and succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete a task is to finish it successfully, which is a synonym of achieving it.

clue.text: Grotesque fish has spiky tail in Lego set

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter
in tells us one piece is placed within the other
set as in arranged, so these letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish, a crossword favourite
the final letter of spiky
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A child builds an ugly spiny-tailed fish from a Lego kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque face or creature on a building, so 'grotesque' as a noun names one.

clue.text: Bit of parsley perhaps cut to hide turnips essentially

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters are used
to hide something is to cover it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a cut is a gash
the central three letters of turnips

explanation.surface: A cook chops parsley to cover up the turnips on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a decorative edible trim on a dish, and a sprig of parsley is a classic example.

clue.text: Daughter invested in dinner gong

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so one letter is set within the other word

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A daughter is honoured at a dinner and the gong is sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or decoration, not the dinner gong the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for an award or decoration, such as a metal disc for honour.

clue.text: Casually look at detective swilling Pinot

indicators.note: swilling means swirling liquid around, so the letters are swished into new places

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
the five letters of Pinot rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective takes a quick look while swirling a glass of Pinot wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into a book is to read bits of it idly, i.e. to browse or look at it casually.

clue.text: Become weaker partner during conflict

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: in bridge, East partners West, so E stands for a partner
a conflict is a war

explanation.surface: A partner grows feeble in the middle of fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, and opposite seats are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear, as in wear thin or wear down, is to deteriorate gradually through use, i.e. weaken.

clue.text: Please, very much credit the French with rosé

blocks.note: buying on tick is buying on credit
le is a French word for the
rosé wine is pink

explanation.surface: Someone asks politely for a lot of credit along with French pink wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like the polite word but is the verb meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To tickle someone pink is an idiom for delighting them greatly, i.e. pleasing them very much.

clue.text: Article on writer has recurring image

blocks.note: the is the definite article
the writer of a clue refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: A piece about an author notes a motif that keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is an idea or motif that recurs throughout a work, much like a repeated image.

clue.text: Half-heartedly intimidate aristocrat

indicators.note: with only half a heart, one of the two central letters is dropped

blocks.note: to nobble is British slang for getting at someone, e.g. a juror, by bribes or threats

explanation.surface: Someone makes a feeble attempt to bully a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of NOBBLE is its middle pair BB; losing half of it removes one B.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a member of the titled upper class, a direct synonym of aristocrat.

clue.text: Kept back spot in nice development for compatriot

indicators.note: kept back suggests held to the rear, so the word runs from its end
in tells us one piece is set inside the other
a development is a change, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: a zit is a pimple, informally a spot
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A spot is kept out of a pleasant building project for a fellow national.
explanation.definitionFit: A compatriot is a fellow citizen of the same country, so citizen fits as a looser synonym.

clue.text: Be ready with key to go in farm building

indicators.note: to go in means to be placed inside, so these letters sit within the outer word

blocks.note: a sty is a pig pen on a farm
with and and both mean along with
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wait with the key for the barn.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand by is a phrasal verb for being prepared to act if needed, i.e. to be ready.

clue.text: Said 'hear, hear!' as financial district expected to ignore president

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: EC is the London postcode of the City, the financial district
to have expected something is to have hoped for it
P is the abbreviation for president, and it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Bankers cheered when the City was expected to snub the president.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, Britain's banking district.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'hear, hear!' repeats agreement with a speaker, so to have done it is to have echoed them.

clue.text: Reportedly secure on dry land

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word is identified by its spoken form

blocks.note: to secure an outcome is to assure it, and that word is pronounced the same in many accents

explanation.surface: Word is that a vessel is safely tied up at the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on the land rather than at sea, the same as being on dry land.
